Looking at the configuration flow, I see 2 things that might be of help here.

1) In `_create_device` a connection with the device is made, to get the mac address from the device itself. This same logic can be used during discovery to get the actual mac address from the device to use as the unique_id.

2) I think you should remove the old Discovery method and clean it from the `discovery` integration, as it now collides with the Zeroconf method. Furthermore, we are trying to get rid of the `discovery` component over time. Netdisco has been deprecated as well.

Also, since you have been using 2 different sources as the unique ID and changing these now, you need to add a migration path for existing entries. Entries with both the hostname & mac exist in the registry, they should be consistent. This can be done on setting up the entry, for example as done here:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/a8e9ccbf1a88d1a9e1c04da36a16910940a9fe19/homeassistant/components/wled/__init__.py#L53-L57

(except in this case, the entry is not None, but contains something else that is not a mac address)

> Looking at the configuration flow, I see 2 things that might be of help here.
> 
> 1. In `_create_device` a connection with the device is made, to get the mac address from the device itself. This same logic can be used during discovery to get the actual mac address from the device to use as the unique_id.

The thing is that for some devices either an API-key or a password is needed to talk to the unit. The code used in netdisco for Daikin discovery does however get mac-address via an UDP-package. We might use that (but I'm not sure what will happen with all models here).

> 2. I think you should remove the old Discovery method and clean it from the `discovery` integration, as it now collides with the Zeroconf method. Furthermore, we are trying to get rid of the `discovery` component over time. Netdisco has been deprecated as well.

Not all units support Zeroconf (but most of them support the discovery from Netdisco).

A unique identifier should not point to 2 different sources, which you kinda figured out at this point 😉 

We cannot discover everything reliably, I think sticking with just Zeroconf makes the most sense. If the unique ID of a device cannot be determined, we should consider it not unique and thus not viable for discovery.

Either way, the current config entries already created now have 2 different identifiers, which should be migrated.

It might be best to just remove all the discovery for this integration, if we can't get a consistent reliable unique id from the device.

If that isn't a breaking change we can even include it in a patch release.

Discovery will only affect new set ups and not existing set ups, correct?

And yes, we need to check and migrate the unique id of the existing entries.
@MartinHjelmare, @frenck I think I've managed to fix the issue now. Would be great with some testers though..
